title: Hopalong Cassidy
paragraphs: William Boyd stars as Hopalong Cassidy, riding with California Carlson through western adventures involving outlaws, mysteries, and frontier justice.
Western adventure starring William Boyd as Hopalong Cassidy and Andy Clyde as California Carlson.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Mutual network (January 1, 1950 to September 24, 1950) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] and CBS network (September 30, 1950 to March 15, 1952) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Clarence Mulford (creator), Ted Bliss (director), William Boyd (performer), Albert Glaser (music director), Walter White Jr. (producer, director, and transcriber), Andy Clyde (performer), and Charles Beldon (performer and screenwriter).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].
The stories often return to murder and violent crime, outlaws and bandits, frontier settlements and trails, gold, mines and treasure, and horses and riding.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Clarence E. Mulford literary origin, Transcribed syndicated radio launch, National network expansion, and Cross-media Hopalong Cassidy boom.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]], [[show|crime-classics|Crime Classics]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|gunsmoke|Gunsmoke]].
